items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Sam has a red kite. He flies it in the park every Saturday.'
Where does Sam fly his kite?
A) At school
B) In the park
C) In his backyard

steps: The text says 'He flies it in the park every Saturday.'

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Butterflies start as tiny eggs. Then they become caterpillars. Next, they form a chrysalis. Finally, they become butterflies.'
What do butterflies start as?
A) Caterpillars
B) Tiny eggs
C) A chrysalis

steps: The text says 'Butterflies start as tiny eggs.'

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'The sun gives us light and heat. It is very far away from Earth.'
What does the sun give us?
A) Rain and snow
B) Light and heat
C) Wind and clouds

steps: The text states 'The sun gives us light and heat.'

items.prompt:
After a read-aloud, a student does not understand a word. She should:
A) Pretend she understood
B) Ask the teacher what the word means
items.answer: B) Ask the teacher what the word means

steps: Asking questions to clarify words or details from a read-aloud is exactly what 1.SL.A.2 expects.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Dogs are loyal animals. They love to play and learn tricks. Most dogs like walks and outdoor time.'
What do most dogs like?
A) Swimming
B) Walks and outdoor time
C) Sleeping all day

steps: The text says 'Most dogs like walks and outdoor time.'

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'The library has thousands of books. You can borrow books and bring them home to read. You must return them in two weeks.'
How long can you keep a library book?
A) One week
B) Two weeks
C) One month

steps: The text says 'You must return them in two weeks.'

items.prompt:
Which is a good question to ask after hearing a story about a penguin?
A) 'What is your favorite animal?'
B) 'Why does a penguin have wings but cannot fly?'
items.answer: B) 'Why does a penguin have wings but cannot fly?'

steps: Option B asks about key details from the story topic (penguins). Option A is a personal opinion question unrelated to the text.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Fire trucks are red and very loud. Firefighters drive them to help put out fires.'
Who drives fire trucks?
A) Police officers
B) Firefighters
C) Teachers

steps: The text says 'Firefighters drive them to help put out fires.'

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Frogs live near water. They eat insects and can jump very far.'
What do frogs eat?
A) Fish
B) Insects
C) Plants

After a teacher reads a story, a student says, 'I don't understand what happened at the end.' What should she do?
A) Forget about it
B) Ask the teacher a question about the ending
items.answer: B) Ask the teacher a question about the ending

steps: Standard 1.SL.A.2: students should ask questions about key details in a text read aloud when they need clarification.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Apples come in red, green, and yellow colors. They grow on trees and are a healthy snack.'
What colors can apples be? (Choose all that apply.)
A) Red, green, and yellow
B) Blue and purple
C) Only red

steps: The text lists three colors: red, green, and yellow.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads a poem. A student wants to ask a question about it. Which question is best?
A) 'Can I go to the bathroom?'
B) 'What did the poet mean by the sun is sleepy?'
items.answer: B) 'What did the poet mean by the sun is sleepy?'

steps: Option B asks about a key detail or image in the poem — it is directly related to the read-aloud content.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'Every year on his birthday, Marcus got a new book from his grandma. He had read all 7 of them by first grade.'
How many books had Marcus read by first grade?
A) 7
B) 8
C) 6

steps: The text says 'He had read all 7 of them by first grade.'

items.prompt:
A teacher reads a nonfiction piece about whales. A student asks, 'How big can a blue whale get?' Is this a good question about the read-aloud?
A) No — it changes the topic.
B) Yes — it asks about a key detail related to the topic.

steps: The text is about whales, so asking about a whale's size is a relevant, key-detail question.

items.prompt:
A teacher reads: 'In the rainforest, it rains almost every single day. The plants grow tall because of all the water and sunlight.'
Why do rainforest plants grow tall?
A) Because of the cold temperatures
B) Because of the water and sunlight
C) Because they are planted by people
items.answer: B) Because of the water and sunlight

steps: The text says 'The plants grow tall because of all the water and sunlight.'
